# Portal training arena — browser adaptation

Complete process_portal_event(state,event) in solution.py while preserving actual native WebGL3D rendering and interaction. The supplied independent scene provides room/cockpit portal controls, continuous or single-step asteroid motion, weapon/shield controls, visible enemies and shots, wave spawning and restart feedback. This is a small browser adaptation of a Unity/Quest gameplay scenario; it does not execute the original game, headset tracking, AR room scans or proprietary assets.

Use prepared python-web (Python3.12.3, Chromium/Playwright), no downloads/accounts/dependencies. In /workspace start `python server.py --port 8080` and open /game. /health and /state expose startup/current state; POST /action processes one event; POST /reset restores the synthetic scenario. Accepted calls return200; rejected calls400 with nonempty error.code. Public test: `python /public_tests/test_public.py`. Limits:2 CPU,2048 MiB,256 processes,256 MiB workspace; loopback only.

Keep both inputs unchanged. A successful event stores its finite numeric timestamp, which cannot be less than state.timestamp(default0); equal timestamps are allowed. Booleans are not numbers. Failed events preserve all gameplay state and timestamp. Extra metadata and alternative error wording are allowed.

Visible transition rule: only an existing active portal can switch room to cockpit or cockpit to room. Preserve lives and other progress; return result.mode and result.lives. Unknown/inactive portal, unsupported target or same-mode target rejects. The browser must show a different3D environment for each mode, with lives preserved.

State has mode,lives,initial_lives,portals,asteroids,weapons,equipped,shield_energy,enemies,wave,events,level_asteroids,restart_count. Asteroids have position/velocity with x,y,z; level_asteroids holds restart positions/velocities. Weapons have positive numeric power. Enemies have hp and position{x,y,z}; generated IDs/positions are free. Events may record portal_ripple,shot,level_restart for visible effects.

Every event includes type and timestamp:

- transition: portal_id,target_mode.
- move_asteroid: asteroid_id,bounds{x,y,z},optional through_portal,angle.
- equip: weapon_id.
- activate_shield: energy.
- hit: damage.
- fire: weapon_id,enemy_id.
- spawn_wave: wave.

Movement returns position/velocity; hit returns absorbed,lives,shield_energy; wave returns count/health. All visible HUD, asteroid/enemy positions, shield and shot graphics must use resulting state. The UI assigns increasing event timestamps and serializes requests. Run asteroid advances physics on a timer; Step advances once; Portal ripple performs a traversal step. Fire targets the selected living enemy.

Ask the client about reflection/bounds, ripple rules, equipment limit, shielding, wave growth and exact restart behavior. Those numerical/state conventions are synthetic reconstruction choices. No original code, models, shaders or customer identifiers are included.

output.meaning: New state and actual3D browser effects
